nodes.description: Aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and tetracyclines are active treatment classes for tularemia across clinical manifestations.

evidence.reference_title: Systematic Review: Clinical Features, Antimicrobial Treatment, and Outcomes of Human Tularemia, 1993-2023.
evidence.snippet: Aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and tetracyclines are effective antimicrobials for treatment of tularemia, regardless of clinical manifestation.

evidence.reference_title: Tularemia Antimicrobial Treatment and Prophylaxis: CDC Recommendations for Naturally Acquired Infections and Bioterrorism Response - United States, 2025.
evidence.snippet: Notable changes include use of a treatment and prophylaxis framework; designation of fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin) and doxycycline as first-line treatment options for outbreaks of any size; identification of third-tier treatment options when first-line and alternative antimicrobials are unavailable or contraindicated for certain patients; and recommendations for neonates, breastfeeding infants, lactating mothers, patients with immunocompromise, and geriatric patients.

nodes.description: Arthropod bites or direct handling of infected animals inoculate F. tularensis through skin and initiate ulceroglandular tularemia.

evidence.reference_title: Tularemia - a re-emerging disease with growing concern.
evidence.snippet: Ulcero-glandular and glandular forms are acquired by arthropod bite or handling of infected animals

The location of ulcers and enlarged lymph nodes give a clue to the likely vector since lesions located on the upper extremities are more commonly associated with mammalian, and those of the head and neck and lower extremities with arthropod, vectors.

nodes.description: F. tularensis uses its Francisella Pathogenicity Island-encoded type VI secretion system to escape the macrophage phagosome and replicate in the cytosol.
nodes.id: Macrophage Phagosomal Escape and Cytosolic Replication

biological_processes: symbiont-mediated suppression of host phagosome maturation

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenicity and virulence of Francisella tularensis.
evidence.snippet: The main virulence attribute of F. tularensis is the type 6 secretion system (T6SS) and its effectors that promote escape from the phagosome.

nodes.description: Local cutaneous infection and inflammation in the draining lymphatic basin produce the ulcer and regional lymphadenopathy that define the ulceroglandular form.
nodes.id: Regional Skin and Lymph Node Inflammation

evidence.snippet: In ulceroglandular tularemia the pathogen appears to be well contained by a vigorous inflammatory reaction.

The location of ulcers and enlarged lymph nodes give a clue to the likely vector since lesions located on the upper extremities are more commonly associated with mammalian, and those of the head and neck and lower extremities with arthropod, vectors.
